Subject: Post-demo: throughput and latency needs for checkout scoring

Thanks again for the demo today — helpful discussion. A quick summary of what we need so we stay aligned: 

- Primary use: real-time checkout fraud scoring (low-latency decisioning called inline).
- Typical steady traffic: ~40–60 RPS, but promo spikes up to 220–300 RPS for short bursts (1–15 minutes).
- Latency targets: p95 <= 90 ms, p99 ideally <= 150 ms (hard requirement: p99 < 200 ms).
- Payload size: average request ~420 tokens (JSON with user/context + SKU embeddings).
- Security: we may require VPC/private options later for certain merchants; for proof-of-concept hosted API is acceptable if you can guarantee isolation controls and audit logs.

Can you confirm what immediate path you recommend (Hosted API vs Dedicated) given the above profile, and a ballpark cost delta? Also we'll share a week of production traces so you can run an early sizing run.

—Laura

Laura — thanks for the clear summary, that helps a lot. High level recommendation based on what you shared:

- Short answer: start with Hosted API for the POC and early ramp, then move to Dedicated capacity when the promo spikes become predictable (sustained peaks >~150 RPS) or when you want strict isolation.

Why: Hosted API gives fastest time-to-value (no infra setup) and we can enable autoscale + burst capacity to handle those short 220–300 RPS spikes. But if you expect consistent peak windows (e.g., every Friday promo traffic is sustained at >150 RPS for hours), Dedicated becomes more cost-effective and gives lower tail latency guarantees.

Immediate asks / next steps I propose: 
1) Please share a redacted 7-day trace (request timestamps + payload sizes) via the secure upload link and confirm any PII restrictions.
2) We will run a perf probe against your traces and return an initial sizing + expected p95/p99 projections (attached: initial-sizing-proposal.xlsx).
3) Karthik will outline a canary plan (small dedicated pool or hosted canary) and an estimated cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted for a 3-month ramp.

If that's agreeable I'll schedule a 30-min tech sync with Karthik and Marissa this week to lock down the trace format and run dates.

Cheers,

Adding a few technical notes for the tech sync / report so we can be precise: 

- For p99 targets under 200 ms with ~420-token payloads, we should instrument KV-cache warmup in the probe. Cold-starts will dominate p99 if invisible in traces.
- Autoscale on Hosted is fine for short bursts but you need 1) fast cell warmup (we can pre-warm pools on predictable promos) and 2) a fallback policy that reroutes to a slightly smaller model variant if tail latency spikes.
- Ballpark compute: assuming nv4-like throughput, to hit median ~40–60 RPS with p95 ~90ms we'd expect a small pool (2–4 instances). For peak 220–300 RPS bursts, autoscale + burst capacity should handle up to ~250 RPS; above that, dedicated reserved nodes will be cheaper.

Options to present to the customer: 
- Hosted POC + Dedicated on ramp: Hosted for 4–6 weeks while we validate, then switch to Dedicated for predictable peaks.
- Dedicated from day 1: if security/VPC is a hard requirement or spikes are extremely frequent.

I'll draft the canary runbook and attach a short latency SLA excerpt you can share with Laura.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Thanks — that sounds reasonable. A couple of clarifications from our side before the sizing run: 

- We will provide a 7-day trace, but note the raw production trace includes user identifiers. We will scrub PII but need to ensure the upload link and handling meet our SOC2 requirements.
- Promo cadence: not every day. Typical big promo windows are ~30–45 minutes, but last quarter we had a 12-minute window that peaked at 310 RPS. For planning, treat 300 RPS as a short-term worst-case spike.
- Tail detail: p95 is normally ~70–85 ms in our current infra; true p99 has been as high as 220 ms under extreme load. Your suggestion to pre-warm sounds important.

Also please send a quick delta estimate (order-of-magnitude) full-month cost for: 1) Hosted API with burst capacity for our profile, and 2) Dedicated reserved pool sized for steady 150 RPS with autoscale headroom for 300 RPS bursts. That will help our finance team pre-approve an initial POC budget.

I'll upload the trace to the secure link once you send it; also we can do the tech sync tomorrow afternoon (PST) if that works for Karthik.

—Laura
